reading.body:
Paul Tonko's AI record is four sponsored or cosponsored bills, four recorded votes, and five $1,000 contributions from Microsoft and Google political committees.

The bills run in one direction. He sponsored the Data Center Fairness Fee Act and the Power for the People Act, and cosponsored the Protecting Families from AI Data Center Energy Costs Act. Three of his four bills name data center power or energy cost in the title, which places him among legislators treating electricity as the point of AI policy rather than a side effect of it. The GUARDRAILS Act is the outlier, a bill about state AI law preemption.

The money is small and repetitive. Five contributions of exactly $1,000, three from Google NETPAC and two from Microsoft's MSVPAC, spread from March 2025 to March 2026. The dates interleave with the bill activity but the data supports no claim about which came first in any causal sense, and the page itself says placement is not a causation claim.

What this does not cover is large. There are no votes on the four bills he sponsored, so nothing here shows whether they advanced. There is no record of committee positions, floor statements, or amendments. The contribution list is limited to AI company and AI-focused committees, so it is not his full fundraising picture. The record shows what he filed and how he voted, not why.
